name: flows and flow router
claim: A cheap router picks a stored flow per case before any provider call, for bootstrap or mid-session, as well as a person would (docs/concepts/FLOWS.md F3).

name: tags and snap policies outside content
claim: Tags, snap policies and transitions stored beside turns attribute turns to many flows with zero bytes added to requests (docs/concepts/FLOWS.md F2).

name: step validators from skills
claim: Step bullets of skills and agent md files can be extracted into validators that check a flow as its turns resolve steps (docs/concepts/FLOWS.md F1).

name: turn templates with fields
claim: Parameterized turn templates with typed fields and validation shapes can be filled by helpers, heuristics or both and pass the same shape (docs/concepts/FLOWS.md F4).

name: turn stack
claim: A pre-allocated stack of templated turns at bootstrap improves quality (completed, first-try edits, nudges, repeats) at equal or lower cost than serial turns, per model (docs/concepts/FLOWS.md F5).

name: turn dithering
claim: Templated turns dispersed by policy keep their allocation guarantee and interleave with flows and checkpoints (docs/concepts/FLOWS.md F6).

name: flow lint
claim: Joining tags, flows, validations and costs shows which hooks and triggers were actionable, and what quality was gained and tokens saved against baselines (docs/concepts/FLOWS.md F7).

name: flows and flow router
claim: A router picks the flow its route rubric names, by logic or agent confidence recorded per pick, pre-provider, with high-level matches typically correct (docs/concepts/FLOWS.md F3).

name: tags and snap policies outside content
claim: Tags, premises and snap policies stay beside the turns, adding zero request bytes by construction, and are easy to gauge, record and verify (docs/concepts/FLOWS.md invariant 1).

name: step validators from skills
claim: Step bullets of skills extract into validators that validate injected turns, drive policies or structure passively, carrying issues and tags to flows, never blocking (docs/concepts/FLOWS.md F1, QF5).

name: turn templates with fields
claim: Template fields fill by helper or by heuristic from the flow's granted role and pass the same validation shape (docs/concepts/FLOWS.md F4).

name: turn stack
claim: Stacks spun up to meet the cache size floor, and a hot agent working from a context pin tapped by micro-requests, deliver quality at lower expense (docs/concepts/FLOWS.md F5).

name: turn dithering
claim: Dithered and saturated-dithered turns keep their policy allocation guarantee and interleave with flows and checkpoints (docs/concepts/FLOWS.md F6).

name: flow lint
claim: Timestamped, state-attributed events join in tandem by query into successes, issues and further strategies without rewriting data (docs/concepts/FLOWS.md F7).

name: quilt and guard
claim: Policy strands form a quilt; a guard resolves out-of-scope events and rejoins the strand, so tags and policies indicate qualifying downstream flows (docs/concepts/FLOWS.md QF3, QF5).

name: seam contracts of policies
claim: Policies indicate model behaviour and so seams; cataloging seams by principle with parameters and return payload shapes gives seam contracts (docs/concepts/FLOWS.md Seam contracts).

name: state-first flow model
claim: Treating tags in force plus flow turn positions as a state, with projections selecting the next transition, lets every hypothesis and lint query be phrased as projected versus occurred (docs/concepts/FLOWS.md State first).

name: semantic-entry handler
claim: A policy-chosen handler that sees only semantic entries, not turns, can pick which turns to stack, in strapped or natural mode, draining a concern queue (docs/concepts/FLOWS.md F9).

name: flow lint
claim: Timestamped, state-attributed events join by query into projected-versus-occurred transitions, successes, issues and further strategies without rewriting data (docs/concepts/FLOWS.md F7, F8).

name: inventory with captures
claim: Enumerating a target's blobs by label with metadata and extracted captures can be built by extraction alone (docs/concepts/INVENTORY.md I1).

name: query shape as the synopsis
claim: Giving the agent a query shape over the inventory lowers repeated reads, since the transition from inventoried to read becomes a capture query (docs/concepts/INVENTORY.md I2).

name: check records and has/has-not view
claim: Check records make what a session has and has not checked answerable from data alone, and are part of the flow state (docs/concepts/INVENTORY.md I3).

name: autonomous inventory leaving seam assertion
claim: An autonomously built inventory leaves only asserting seams and inferring interface points and domain contracts (docs/concepts/INVENTORY.md I4).

name: network inventory
claim: One IaC source yields a network inventory (ranges, rules, allow and deny lists) by extraction alone (docs/concepts/INVENTORY.md I5).
